ts vector¶

vector models several series together. A vector autoregression (Var) makes each series a linear function of the past of all of them; its fit offers impulse responses, forecast-error variance decompositions, Granger tests and forecasts. When the series have unit roots but share long-run relations (cointegration), johansen_test finds how many relations there are and Vecm fits the error-correction form; var_to_vecm and vecm_to_var convert between the two representations.

Series are given as an n × k matrix with one column per series. Coefficient arrays use the row-vector convention: ar[l][j][i] is the effect of series j at lag l + 1 on series i, and the impulse responses and variance shares are indexed [step][shock][response].

How To Call It¶

Fit a VAR(1) to two linked series, read the first-lag coefficients and forecast.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n, int offset) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + offset + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
// Two linked series: a_t = 0.5 a_{t-1} + 0.2 b_{t-1} + e1_t,  b_t = 0.1 a_{t-1} + 0.6 b_{t-1} + 0.5 e1_t + e2_t   (n x 2, row t = (a_t, b_t)).
Series linked(int n) {
  const auto e1 = noise(n, 0), e2 = noise(n, 5000);
  std::vector<double> y(2 * n);
  double a = 0.0, b = 0.0;
  for (int t = 0; t < n; ++t) {
    const double na = 0.5 * a + 0.2 * b + e1[t];
    const double nb = 0.1 * a + 0.6 * b + 0.5 * e1[t] + e2[t];
    a = na;
    b = nb;
    y[2 * t] = a;
    y[2 * t + 1] = b;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(y, {n, 2}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = linked(300);
  const auto fit = ts::Var::fit_mle(y);
  const Series a1 = fit.ar.select(0, 0);
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "effect of series 0 on (0, 1): " << a1.select(0, 0).host<double>()[0] << ", " << a1.select(0, 0).host<double>()[1] << "\n";
  std::cout << "effect of series 1 on (0, 1): " << a1.select(0, 1).host<double>()[0] << ", " << a1.select(0, 1).host<double>()[1] << "\n";
  show("forecast row 1", fit.forecast(2, y).select(0, 0));
}

Output

effect of series 0 on (0, 1): 0.5210, 0.1654
effect of series 1 on (0, 1): 0.1466, 0.5387
forecast row 1   0.0149   0.0190
